summary: LDAP bind DN with unescaped '#' in on-prem IdP causes group sync to drop on region failover, blocking tenant admins
description:
Issue summary:
NimbleFinance reported that after a scheduled control-plane failover (eu-west primary -> eu-west-failover) their tenant administrators lost admin privileges in the private deployment. Affected users could authenticate but RBAC group memberships were not applied, causing 403s on admin routes and failing scheduled ingestion jobs that use delegated admin tokens.

Impact:
- Tenant admin UI shows 'Insufficient permissions' for multiple users (5 admins affected).
- Daily scheduled ingestion jobs failed (5/5) over the failover window.
- Customer-facing apps with webhook provisioning experienced delayed processing (~3 hours).

Environment:
- Private control plane running v2025.11.3 on customer-managed VMs behind an on-prem edge proxy.
- LDAP: Microsoft AD (on-prem), single forest, referral chasing enabled.
- Failover executed using documented failover playbook at 2026-03-10T02:12:00Z.
steps_to_reproduce: Perform control-plane failover per runbook (primary -> standby) in eu-west on a deployment that uses LDAP with referral-chasing enabled.
Trigger a full resync of group bindings (Config > Auth > Sync Groups) or allow automatic post-failover sync.

Attempt to perform an admin-only action (tenant settings, user impersonation) as an admin user whose account is bound by an LDAP group with a DN containing a '#' character in the bind DN upstream metadata.
Observe 403 responses on admin API and missing group entries in /admin/tenants/{id}/bindings.
Check LDAP connector logs and control-plane auth logs for parsing errors.
logs: 2026-03-10T02:14:12Z auth-svc ERROR: group-sync failed for tenant 'nimblefinance' - ldap bind DN parse error: unexpected token '#' in DN 'CN=Sync Service#01,OU=Service Accounts,DC=nimble,DC=local'
2026-03-10T02:14:13Z ldap-connector WARN: referral-chase starting for base 'DC=partners,DC=corp'
2026-03-10T02:14:13Z ldap-connector ERROR: startTLS: bind failed: invalid DN format
2026-03-10T02:15:40Z control-plane INFO: user 'alice.n@nimblefinance' authenticated (id=10042) but effective groups=[] - expected groups=['tenant-admin']
comments: Support (Ava Patel) 2026-03-10T03:05:12Z: Received initial report from NimbleFinance via support@. Customer says failover completed and then tenant admins lost admin privileges. Asked for LDAP connector and auth logs; requested last successful sync timestamp.

Customer (NimbleFinance - Jose Mendez) 2026-03-10T03:22:01Z: Provided LDAP config snippet and indicated the service account DN has a '#' character because their onboarding script appends an environment tag (e.g., 'Sync Service#01'). They confirmed the DN works from their AD tools.

SRE (Ravi Sharma) 2026-03-10T04:45:30Z: Reproduced bind DN parse error in staging when LDAP connector hits an unescaped '#'. When referral chasing is enabled the connector re-encodes/refollows referrals and triggers a path where DN parsing uses our internal DN tokenizer which treats '#' as a comment/start-of-escaped-value. Filing with infra to hotfix parser tolerant behavior.

Support (Ava Patel) 2026-03-11T09:12:14Z: Applied short-term workaround for customer: modified their LDAP connector configuration to disable referral chasing and restarted connector; initiated manual full group resync; admins regained permissions within ~8 minutes. Customer confirmed scheduled jobs retried successfully.

Engineering (Samantha Liu) 2026-03-12T14:28:02Z: Root cause confirmed: LDAP DN tokenizer in private-deploy runtime incorrectly treats unescaped '#' as a DN comment per RFC2253 edge-case when referral-chasing codepath uses alternative parsing library. Patch PR prepared to normalize/escape '#' in bind DN and to accept both escaped and unescaped forms when reading upstream metadata.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Edge proxy rewrites DN or header, inserting unescaped characters -> verified false: packet captures show DN header intact across proxy.

Hypothesis 2: Referral chasing causes alternate codepath in LDAP connector that uses a third-party DN parser with stricter grammar -> reproduced locally and confirmed. Third-party parser rejects '#' unless escaped as '\#'.
Correlation: Tenants using referral-chasing + service account DNs with '#' impacted; tenants without '#' or with escaped '#' were not impacted.

Logs show successful authentication but group membership empty (groups=[]). That indicates bind succeeded for authentication path but group enumeration (separate bind) failed in the connector's referral-return path.
Tested workaround: disable referral-chasing -> group sync proceeds (slower) because connector fetches local partitions only but succeeds because DN parsing codepath doesn't run.
root_cause: LDAP connector's referral-chase codepath uses a stricter DN parser that rejects unescaped '#' in bind DNs. During failover a connector restart triggered a resync using referral-chasing, exposing the parser mismatch and dropping group resolution leading to lost RBAC bindings.
resolution:
Short-term: Disabled referral-chasing in the customer's LDAP connector config and performed manual full group resync; verified tenancy admin privileges restored and scheduled jobs retried successfully.
Long-term: Engineering has merged a patch that normalizes/accepts '#' in bind DNs and updates the referral-chase parser. Patch will be included in v2026.04.1 for private deployments. Recommended customer follow-up: re-enable referral-chasing after patch rollout and run a scheduled group sync.
Rollout notes: Patch requires connector restart; rolling upgrade plan provided to customer to avoid prolonged window. Scheduled patch window proposed: 2026-03-20 02:00-03:00 UTC.
follow_up_actions: ENG: Monitor post-patch customer telemetry for 72 hours after enabling referral-chasing (owner: Samantha Liu)
SUPPORT: Confirm customer's IAM runbook includes escaping recommendations for generated service account DNs (owner: Ava Patel)
SRE: Add a health check to detect DN-parse failures during group-sync and alert early (owner: Ravi Sharma)
